sources.title: Jason D. Lee, Dennis L. Sun, Yuekai Sun, and Jonathan E. Taylor, Exact Post-Selection Inference, with Application to the Lasso
sources.locator: Complete PDF pp. 1–22. Load-bearing ranges: Lemma 5.1 and its rowwise proof, pp. 11–12; Theorem 5.2 and conditional-uniform proof, pp. 12–13; Theorem 6.1, pp. 14–15; Appendix A, p. 20.
sources.read_status: Complete source document inspected page by page, PDF pp. 1–22.

contents.name: Lemma 2.1: conditional coverage implies false-coverage-rate control
contents.reason: This batch proves one fixed contrast after one fixed event; familywise and false-coverage-rate aggregation are not part of the assigned theorem.

contents.name: Lemma 4.1 and Proposition 4.2: lasso selection can be represented by affine inequalities
contents.reason: The assigned input already is an arbitrary fixed polyhedron; deriving the lasso-specific selection event would add a different selection algorithm.

contents.name: Lemma 5.1: a single polyhedron restricts the contrast to an interval
contents.reason: The A-page lemma rederives the rowwise positive, negative, and zero-coefficient cases with the isotropic contrast projection used by this plan.

contents.name: Theorem 5.2: the truncated-normal conditional CDF is uniform
contents.reason: The A-page theorem proves the conditional density kernel and the probability-integral transform locally, including zero-normalizer fibers.

contents.name: Theorem 5.3: conditioning on a union of polyhedra
contents.reason: The design fixes one event {AY≤b}; it explicitly does not claim the union-of-polyhedra or selected-model-only extension.

contents.name: Theorem 6.1: exact confidence inversion and the interval-shape assertion
contents.reason: The local corollary proves exact central pivot inversion; it does not claim the stronger interval-shape conclusion that uses the separate monotone-likelihood-ratio argument.

contents.name: Appendix A, Lemma A.1: monotonicity in the truncated-normal mean
contents.reason: The assigned claim is exact confidence-set coverage and does not assert unique interval endpoints or that the inverted set must be connected.

contents.name: Section 8.1: plug-in unknown-variance extensions
contents.reason: The controlling design requires known positive variance and excludes both asymptotic plug-in validity and conservative variance overestimation.

sources.title: William Fithian, Dennis L. Sun, and Jonathan E. Taylor, Optimal Inference After Model Selection
sources.locator: Focused reading: PDF pp. 1–10 and 15–16. Selective type-I error and conditioning, pp. 3–8; test/confidence-set duality, p. 9; finer-selection monotonicity, p. 10; conditional exponential family and UMPU tests, pp. 15–16.
sources.read_status: Focused source ranges inspected: PDF pp. 1–10 and 15–16. Other pages were not used.

contents.name: Selective type-I-error definition conditional on the question being asked
contents.reason: The corollary states p-value validity and the rejection bound under the conditional laws Q_mu=P_mu(.|S) for each fixed contrast.

contents.name: Example 1: the file-drawer selection effect
contents.reason: This is a motivation about repeated reporting across studies; the assigned B example is the two-normal-means polyhedral event.

contents.name: Proposition 2: selective test and confidence-set duality
contents.reason: The corollary inverts the central acceptance set and proves its exact conditional coverage for the contrast functional.

contents.name: Proposition 3: error monotonicity under finer selection variables
contents.reason: The result compares power and error guarantees across selection partitions; this batch proves one conditional pivot without such a comparison.

contents.name: Theorem 5 and Corollary 6: uniformly most powerful unbiased selective tests
contents.reason: The assigned equal-tailed pivot test is exact but no unbiasedness, admissibility, or optimal-power claim is included.

contents.name: Section 3.1, conditional exponential-family representation
contents.reason: The local proof derives the selected conditional law directly from the product density rather than importing the general exponential-family statement.

sources.read_status: Complete 48-slide PDF inspected through its extracted full-text rendering.

contents.name: General affine selection event representation, slide 7
contents.reason: The local setup defines one fixed selection event {Ay≤b}; no algorithm is assumed to generate the event.

contents.name: Lasso-specific KKT selection event construction, slides 8–15
contents.reason: The assigned contract begins with an arbitrary fixed polyhedron and does not construct lasso or forward-stepwise selection events.

contents.name: Polyhedral lemma and interval proof, slides 17–20
contents.reason: The local interval proof is complete. The deck's displayed general-covariance coefficient c=(eta^T Sigma^{-1} eta)^{-1}Sigma eta does not satisfy eta^T c=1 in general, so that coefficient is not used; the isotropic c=eta/||eta||^2 is derived locally.

contents.name: Truncated-normal conditional CDF and equal-tailed confidence intervals, slides 20–22
contents.reason: The local theorem establishes the CDF formula and conditional uniformity; the lecture's univariate CDF display is used only as an independent cross-check.

contents.name: Union-of-polyhedra conditioning on coefficient signs, slides 24–25
contents.reason: The assigned theorem conditions on one fixed polyhedron and does not include the union-of-polyhedra extension.

contents.name: Unknown-variance estimation and plug-in confidence intervals, slides 27–28
contents.reason: Known variance is an explicit hypothesis; no estimated-variance or asymptotic selective guarantee is claimed.

contents.name: Selective inference for hierarchical clustering, slides 32–46
contents.reason: Clustering selection and its truncated chi-square law are a separate model-specific topic outside the fixed Gaussian polyhedron contract.

contents.name: Conditional-inference limitations, slides 47–48
contents.reason: The A-page scope records that the conditional guarantee assumes the stated Gaussian model and fixed event, and proves no model-adequacy or robustness conclusion.
